preserved_prior_findings.stage_x_refined_formula: B AND (A OR (C AND D AND E))
preserved_prior_findings.A: target-side same-logical-effect idempotent replay/correlation or target-enforced exclusive fencing
preserved_prior_findings.B: authoritative positive committed-effect visibility bound to the logical generation
preserved_prior_findings.C: authoritative negative closure proving an ambiguous attempt did not commit and cannot later commit
preserved_prior_findings.D: attempt-generation identity/freshness preventing stale B/C witnesses from affecting another generation
preserved_prior_findings.E: durable pre-attempt ARMED_k reservation plus exact readback before any non-idempotent launch; recovered ARMED/LAUNCH_CLAIMED remains UNKNOWN-equivalent until matching B(k) or C(k)

bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Deterministic local acceptance-matrix construction only. It specifies the observations and falsifiers required to qualify one future concrete Chat-capable target primitive against A or authoritative B/C with D/E binding. No public source, target mutation, protected authority, manual execution, hosted compute, quota-bearing feature, O/downstream/other-worker semantic input, or legacy research was used in the valid frozen-authority slice.

required_observations: A caller-visible logical generation/correlation key or target-enforced fence is accepted before the effect.
Replaying the same logical generation after an ambiguous transport/crash cannot produce a second logical effect, not merely a second request record.
The protection scope/window is long enough to cover cross-invocation recovery or is target-persistent rather than an undocumented transient cache.
falsifiers: The same generation can produce two logical effects.
The key/fence only deduplicates transport while allowing duplicate logical commits.
Protection expires before safe cross-run recovery without authoritative closure.
Using the primitive requires richer-mode/protected/manual execution, finite hosted quota, or incremental monetary cost.

required_observations: The target exposes an authoritative committed-effect witness keyed to generation k or an equivalent immutable correlation.
A recovered Chat invocation can read that witness without executing the effect again.
The witness identifies the logical effect rather than only request receipt/queue acceptance.
falsifiers: Only client-side acknowledgement, timeout absence, or repository intent state is visible.
The status cannot be bound to generation k.
Positive visibility requires a residual executor or quota-bearing service unavailable at zero quota.

required_observations: For ambiguous attempt k, the target can prove that k did not commit and cannot later commit.
Closure is terminal and generation-bound rather than inferred from elapsed time or missing B(k).
After C(k), a fresh generation may be armed without violating the no-overlap invariant.
falsifiers: Timeout, not-found, queue disappearance, or absence of B is treated as C.
A late commit remains possible after claimed closure.
Closure is not bound to k or can be satisfied by stale evidence.

required_observations: D binds every A/B/C witness to the current generation k and rejects stale-generation evidence.
E persists ARMED_k before the first non-idempotent launch and exact-reads it back.
Recovered ARMED_k or LAUNCH_CLAIMED_k without matching B(k)/C(k) is treated as UNKNOWN, never as permission to relaunch.
falsifiers: A witness for generation j can resolve k.
The first launch can occur before durable E readback.
Repository ownership/nonce alone is treated as proof of target-side launch or non-launch.

required_observations: All required reads/writes are exposed to scheduled Chat through lightweight transport/state APIs.
The accepted path works with optional monthly/trial/paid compute, artifact, cloud-credit, hosted-runner and similar quotas set to zero.
Incremental monetary cost is zero and no protected/manual/richer-mode execution remains in the outcome path.
falsifiers: A user, protected worker, richer execution mode, hosted runner, finite credit, or paid service must finish the effect/recovery.
The primitive is only inspectable but not safely usable from scheduled Chat.
Zero-quota operation removes any required A/B/C/D/E capability.

bounded_leaf_result.decision_rule: A future concrete primitive may qualify only within its exact tested scope. Positive recovery architecture requires authoritative B plus either target-side A, or target-side C together with D and E. If neither A nor authoritative C is source/test qualified, the state remains unresolved and repository-only relaunch is forbidden. Timeout or missing B never substitutes for C.
bounded_leaf_result.first_falsification_priority: Test same-generation duplicate-effect behavior for A candidates, or late-commit-after-negative-closure behavior for C candidates, before claiming a primitive can close the crash window.
